joins.note: Jung names feeling the third of four functions of orientation, which states whether a thing suits us or not (CW11 ¶246).

cites.quote: So, too, there are four aspects of psychological orientation, beyond which nothing fundamental remains to be said.

In order to orient ourselves, we must have a function which ascertains that something is there (sensation); a second function which establishes what it is (thinking); a third function which states whether it suits us or not, whether we wish to accept it or not (feeling); and a fourth function which indicates where it came from and where it is going (intuition).

joins.note: Burt calls Virgo the Earth sign, ruled by Hermes (pdf p211).

cites.quote: As ruler of the Earth sign Virgo, Hermes seems less flighty, more grounded, stable and consistent in his behavior than he was as ruler of airy Gemini.
The earthy nature of Virgo seems to provide Hermes the patience and powers of concentration required for his serious healing and alchemical work.

joins.note: Burt names Virgo-Pisces among the opposites whose tension brings perspective, growth and wisdom (pdf p13).

cites.quote: From the tension between the opposites (Aries-Libra, Taurus-Scorpio, Gemini-Sagittarius, Cancer-Capricorn, Leo-Aquarius, Virgo-Pisces), perspective, growth, and wisdom comes.
One of the six axes of the horoscope wheel consisting of 2 houses or signs—a continuum from Earth/Water or Air/Fire to be brought into balanced perspective.

joins.note: Maier, quoted by Jung, puts the spirit in lunar whiteness, like water (CW12 note 41, pdf p648).

joins.note: Jung writes of four elements, water among them (CW12 ¶333); the fourth is sometimes earth, sometimes fire (CW12 ¶31).

cites.quote: Whereas the original tetrameria corresponded exactly to the quaternity of elements, it was now frequently stressed that although there were four elements (earth, water, fire, and air) and four qualities (hot, cold, dry, and moist), there were only three colours: black, white, and red.
There are always four elements, but often three of them are grouped together, with the fourth in a special position—sometimes earth, sometimes fire.
